title: Power Pages: client APIs for scripting forms, lists, users and data
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licensing requirements and server-side permission boundaries are supported. Both admin paths reach the correct pages but should include the final steps for editing the controls.

claims.claim: Power Pages provides a documented JavaScript client API for developers customising site pages.
claims.quote: Power Pages client APIs help developers manipulate UI components, manage forms and lists, handle user authentication, and interact with Dataverse records programmatically.

claims.claim: The client API can retrieve and change forms.
claims.quote: Retrieve and modify forms and form controls

claims.claim: The client API can retrieve and change form controls.
claims.quote: Retrieve and modify forms and form controls

claims.claim: The client API can read and style rows and cells in modern lists.
claims.quote: Read and style rows, columns, and cells in modern lists

claims.claim: $pages.user.signIn redirects the user to the sign-in page.
claims.quote: `signIn` | Redirects the user to the sign-in page.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: $pages.user.signOut signs out the currently signed-in user.
claims.quote: `signOut` | Signs out the currently signed-in user.

claims.claim: $pages.webAPI provides operations on Dataverse records.
claims.quote: Use the Power Pages Client API `$pages.webAPI` object to create, retrieve, update, and delete Dataverse records and to work with content stored in file and image columns.

claims.claim: The client API works with files stored in Dataverse file columns.
claims.quote: Use the Power Pages Client API `$pages.webAPI` object to create, retrieve, update, and delete Dataverse records and to work with content stored in file and image columns.

claims.claim: The client API works with images stored in Dataverse image columns.
claims.quote: You can use this method with image columns.

claims.claim: $pages.ajax can call server endpoints and cloud flows.
claims.quote: Use it to call server logic, cloud flows, and other custom `/_api/` endpoints from client scripts.

claims.claim: $pages.agent provides communication with Microsoft Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: Use the Power Pages Client API `$pages.agent` object and its SendActivity method to send messages or invoke events in the Microsoft Copilot Studio agent available to the current user.

claims.claim: The client API overview includes languages and multilingual content.
claims.quote: Work with multilingual content

claims.claim: The roadmap presents client APIs as a supported alternative to fragile DOM manipulation.
claims.quote: Power Pages Client APIs address these challenges by offering stable, documented, and supported methods to interact with components, reducing risk, improving maintainability, and accelerating development.

claims.claim: Microsoft.PowerPages.onPagesClientApiReady supplies the API object after initialisation is complete.
claims.quote: Use the `Microsoft.PowerPages.onPagesClientApiReady` function to assign the API object to `$pages` when it's ready, so your scripts can access page APIs only after initialization completes.

claims.claim: The Learn overview says the client API becomes available when the page loads.
claims.quote: The client API becomes available when your page loads and can be accessed through a global variable with a name you choose.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The described site changes require developer-written client API calls; visitors see the results of that script.
claims.quote: Each example is complete, so you can copy it into a JavaScript web file or into the **Custom JavaScript** section of a page, and then change the form names, column names, and table names to match your site.

claims.claim: No administrator action is required to make the capability available.
claims.quote: Enabled for end users automatically

claims.quote: Power Pages enforces table permissions on the server.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The client API cannot override server-side table permissions.
claims.quote: Power Pages applies form metadata and table permissions on the server, and the client API can't override those settings.

claims.claim: $pages.webAPI.retrieveRecord retrieves a record by its unique identifier.

claims.claim: $pages.webAPI.retrieveMultipleRecords retrieves records using query options.
claims.quote: `retrieveMultipleRecords` | Retrieves multiple records based on the provided query options.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: $pages.webAPI.deleteRecord deletes a record.

claims.claim: $pages.webAPI supports file upload.
claims.quote: `uploadFileToColumn` | Uploads a file or an image to a file column or an image column of an existing record.

claims.claim: $pages.webAPI supports file download.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Associated web roles and table permissions bound which records and operations a site's Web API user can access.
claims.quote: The portal Web API accesses table (entity) records and follows the table permissions given to users through the associated web role.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Granting the Anonymous users web role table access makes that data accessible to any visitor, including through permitted Web API calls.
claims.quote: When the Anonymous users web role is granted access to a table, any user who visits the site can access the data in the table.

claims.claim: The tenant Anonymous access to Dataverse control can override maker permissions and block anonymous reads.
claims.quote: Selecting All sites blocks anonymous access in all the websites in the tenant, overriding any maker configurations that provide access to anonymous users.

claims.claim: Blocking anonymous reads with that setting does not prevent unauthenticated users writing Dataverse data.
claims.quote: While unauthenticated users will be prevented from viewing Dataverse data when this setting is enabled, these users can still write data to Dataverse.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: setVisible(false) on a control hides it in the browser rather than securing its data.
claims.quote: The `setVisible(false)` method hides a control in the browser only. Use table permissions and column security to protect data. Never rely on hiding a control to secure data.

claims.claim: row.setVisible(false) changes only the displayed list, not its server-returned data.
claims.quote: Hiding a row changes only what people see in the list; it doesn't change the data or the number of records that the server returns.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn instructs developers to protect data with table permissions and column security rather than by hiding controls.
claims.quote: Use table permissions and column security to protect data. Never rely on hiding a control to secure data.

claims.claim: The client API user reference gives no method for changing the site's accepted identity providers.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages client API user signIn signOut identity providers configuration methods. Opened client-api/user-authentication: only signIn and signOut; search results locate provider configuration in Security > Identity providers, not $pages.user.

claims.claim: $pages.ajax.request automatically adds the CSRF token to every request.
claims.quote: The token is retrieved when it's first needed, cached in memory, and added to the header of every request.

claims.claim: $pages.ajax.request includes the session cookie, running requests in the visitor's session.
claims.quote: Credentials: The session cookie is included with every request.

claims.claim: Client script can call /_api/serverlogics/ endpoints.
claims.quote: `url` | string | Yes | A relative path, such as `/_api/serverlogics/mylogic`, or an absolute URL.

claims.claim: Client script can trigger cloud flows registered with the site.
claims.quote: Trigger a cloud flow | Triggers a cloud flow registered with the site and handles the flow response.

claims.claim: $pages.agent.SendActivity sends a message or invokes an event in a specified Copilot Studio agent.
claims.quote: The `SendActivity` method sends a message or invokes an event in the specified Copilot Studio agent and uses callback functions to handle responses and errors.

claims.claim: Agent access permissions are checked for the current user.
claims.quote: Invalid bot schema name provided or user doesn't have access permissions to the agent

claims.claim: getRecordCount returns a maximum count of 5,000.
claims.quote: The server returns a maximum count of 5,000. When a table contains more than 5,000 records, the result is 5,000.

claims.claim: Learn recommends retrieveMultipleRecords with $count=true for records together with their total in @odata.count.
claims.quote: To retrieve records together with their total count, use the retrieveMultipleRecords method with the `$count=true` query option instead. That method returns the collection in the `value` property of the response, and the total count in the `@odata.count` property.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The seven cited client API pages name no licence, price, meter or separate client-API charge.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages client APIs licence prerequisites price meter licensing. Opened overview, initialization, dataverse, user-authentication, ajax, agents and examples; none names a licence, price or meter. Product licensing is separately documented in the licensing FAQs.

claims.claim: The cited client API reference pages list no prerequisite licence or administrator role.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages client APIs licence prerequisites price meter licensing. Opened overview, initialization, dataverse, user-authentication, ajax, agents and examples; no prerequisite licence or administrator role is listed.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Pages has authenticated-user capacity per website per month.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Pages has anonymous-user capacity per website per month.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.

claims.claim: Power Pages offers both subscription capacity and pay-as-you-go licensing options.
claims.quote: The Authenticated user capacity subscription license can be purchased ... The Authenticated user pay-as-you-go meter enables customers to pay-as-you-go based on the actual number of authenticated users who have accessed a website in a month.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, reflecting the documented subscription and pay-as-you-go options.
claims.quote: Subscription and pay-as-you-go pricing is detailed below.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Portals Web API operations require a Power Pages licence.
claims.quote: Portals Web API operations require a Power Pages license.

claims.claim: Anonymous Web API calls count towards anonymous-user capacity.
claims.quote: Web API calls made by anonymous users count towards the anonymous user capacity.

claims.claim: Authenticated Web API calls require applicable authenticated-user capacity licences.
claims.quote: Web API calls made by authenticated users (internal or external) don't count towards page views, but require applicable authenticated user capacity licenses.

claims.claim: The portals Web API capacity requirements apply to $pages.webAPI calls, which Microsoft identifies as Power Pages Web API calls.
claims.quote: Review the client-side code and other site components that call the Power Pages Web API. Common call patterns include: ... $pages.webAPI.retrieveRecord(...) ... $pages.webAPI.retrieveMultipleRecords(...)

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Cloud flow integration with Power Pages requires a Power Automate licence.
claims.quote: To integrate with Power Pages, a Power Automate license is required.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends a Power Automate Process licence for the production instance.
claims.quote: It's recommended to use a Power Automate Process license in the production instance.

claims.claim: The client API agent page does not cover licensing for Copilot Studio agents called through $pages.agent.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages client APIs licence prerequisites price meter licensing. Opened client-api/agents in full; it documents SendActivity, callbacks and errors, but no agent licensing requirement.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Webapi/<table-name>/enabled controls whether a table's Web API is enabled, and the troubleshooting page tells readers to verify True.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Webapi/<table-name>/fields exposes an explicit comma-separated list of column logical names for $pages.webAPI calls.
claims.quote: Replace `*` with a comma-separated list of column logical names. ... Common call patterns include: ... $pages.webAPI.retrieveRecord(...) ... $pages.webAPI.retrieveMultipleRecords(...)

claims.claim: The fields list can be combined with Webapi/<table-name>/UseFieldsFromView.
claims.quote: If both settings are configured, the Web API combines the columns listed in `Webapi/<table-name>/fields` with eligible columns from the Power Pages Web API Columns system view for that table.

claims.claim: UseFieldsFromView is available in Power Pages site version 9.8.8.x and later.
claims.quote: The `Webapi/<table-name>/UseFieldsFromView` site setting is available in Power Pages site version 9.8.8.x and later.

claims.claim: The wildcard value * is not supported on any website starting 14 September 2026.
claims.quote: Starting September 14, 2026, the wildcard value isn't supported on any website.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The client API reference pages themselves omit the Webapi table enabled and fields site settings.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages client API disable turn off admin switch site settings onPagesClientApiReady. Opened client-api overview, initialization, dataverse, user-authentication, ajax, agents and examples; none names Webapi/<table-name>/enabled or Webapi/<table-name>/fields.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and controls[2].api; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No tenant or site switch specifically disabling the client API itself is documented on either the admin UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages client API disable enable site setting Power Platform API pac pages admin PowerShell. Read client-api, configure-site-settings, power-platform-cli and search excerpts for admin-api and pac power-pages; found site-wide controls, not a client-API-specific switch.

claims.claim: setDisabled is not a substitute for server-enforced rules and cannot unlock a server-locked control.
claims.quote: When a control is locked on the server, such as a multiselect picklist on a read-only form or field, the `setDisabled(false)` method has no effect.
